stories.title: US offers up to $20 million for tips on Iran's nuclear programme
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department announced a Rewards for Justice offer of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear programme, and said the informant could be offered relocation assistance. The announcement follows former President Donald Trump’s claim that a U.S.–Israel bombing campaign had completely destroyed Iran’s nuclear facilities, a claim Iran rejects, maintaining its programme is peaceful. The U.S. military also said it is forming a task force to curb the movement of weapons and sanctioned material across Iran’s borders.
stories.why: The reward is intended to generate intelligence that could aid U.S. efforts to monitor and counter Iran’s nuclear activities.

stories.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion in new funding round, valuation $1.25 trillion
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported, via TechCrunch, that OpenAI has secured $11 billion so far in an ongoing financing round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The round has not closed and Bloomberg said it could total about $20 billion, below the roughly $30 billion target mentioned in September. TechCrunch has asked OpenAI for comment.
stories.why: The capital could fund OpenAI’s product development and affect its competitive positioning.

stories.title: Concurrent Gainers: 9 stocks gain for 5 days in a row
stories.summary: Amid this broad-based rally, around 45 stocks from the BSE 200 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 2 to 6. Of these, we shortlisted 9 stocks that consistently gained throughout the period, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 15% to 20%.

stories.title: Crusoe sells unfinished Wyoming data center project to Google
stories.summary: Crusoe, a Denver‑based data‑center developer valued at $30.9 billion, confirmed it has sold an unfinished data‑center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which had previously tried to become a customer, is taking over the development after raising concerns about cost and timeline under Crusoe’s management. Google announced a $17 billion investment to build the campus, a project originally announced with Tallgrass and intended to scale to 10 GW of power capacity.
stories.why: The deal illustrates the difficulties independent developers face with large‑scale data‑center builds and signals Google’s ongoing expansion of its infrastructure footprint.
